passage:
The dholak was so loud in the wedding hall that Salma held her phone against one ear and her palm against the other. The newest voice note from her best friend Hrithik was six minutes long. She caught only "...and then the buffalo, Salma, the buffalo sat in the road and..." followed by his laughing.
She typed instead: "Hriii I am at a wedding, can't hear a word 😊 will listen tonight!"
Hrithik grinned at his phone. He had not thought about where she might be. He sent back, "No rush! Just wanted you to hear the buffalo story 😄 tell me when you're free." Later that night Salma listened with earphones, laughing under her blanket.

qa.q: How long was Hrithik's voice note?
qa.a: Hrithik's voice note was six minutes long.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling as he read Salma's reply, and what shows it?
qa.a: Hrithik felt amused and relaxed. He grinned and sent a friendly answer, since he simply had not thought about where Salma might be.

qa.q: What small habit could Hrithik add before sending a long voice note?
qa.a: Hrithik could ask if Salma is free to listen, or leave the note to be played whenever she can. That respects her time and setting and keeps the fun.

qa.q: What was it like for Salma to receive the note in the wedding hall?
qa.a: Salma could not hear it over the dholak and had to press the phone against one ear. She still wanted the buffalo story, so she promised to listen at night.

grounding: A teenager sends a long, laughing voice note to a close friend who is at a loud wedding and cannot listen, then finds a kind arrangement.

passage:
Ojas lay on the terrace mat, phone above his face, ready to send his best friend Jatin a note. He pressed record.
"Jatin, listen, you will not believe this, the auto driver today told me his meter has a personality and I said..." He broke off, snorting, and rambled on about the driver, the mango stall and his cousin's terrible singing. When he stopped, the note was four minutes and twelve seconds.
Across town, Jatin was on his own balcony with earphones in, since the flat was asleep. He listened, laughing into his sleeve, and pressed record. "Okay, my turn. I have to whisper, it's late..."
They traded notes until the stars faded, each one longer than the last.

qa.q: Where was Ojas lying when he recorded the voice note?
qa.a: Ojas was lying on the terrace mat.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling as the words tumbled out in the recording?
qa.a: Ojas felt amused and excited, snorting with laughter and rambling from the driver to the mango stall. The note ran over four minutes because Ojas was enjoying it.

qa.q: What made it easy for Jatin to enjoy the note, and what could help Ojas next time?
qa.a: Jatin had earphones and privacy since the flat was asleep. Ojas could check that Jatin has a quiet moment, so the note is enjoyed and not forced.

qa.q: What is it like for Jatin to receive Ojas's note on the balcony?
qa.a: Jatin is at ease and delighted, laughing into a sleeve and answering straight away. With earphones in and the flat asleep, Jatin has the privacy to enjoy it.

grounding: A teenager sends long, rambling, laughing voice notes to a close friend who replies in kind, on a quiet night with earphones.

passage:
Yusuf lay on his bed in the Hyderabad flat, phone close to his mouth, laughing so hard he had to stop the recording twice. Four minutes about the gully cricket match: the ball in Mrs Reddy's balcony, the dog that stole the stumps, his own dramatic slip. He sent it to Rehana, then another two minutes because he'd forgotten the best part.
Rehana was at her aunt's dinner table. The phone buzzed twice. She pressed play under the table, meaning to hear only a few seconds, and Yusuf's laugh blasted out: "And then I fell flat, like a sack of onions!"
Her aunt raised an eyebrow. Her cousins stared.
Later she sent a voice note back, whispering from the balcony. "Your story was the best thing today. But next time, text me 'long voice note, funny, no hurry' first. My aunt now thinks you're a sack of onions."
Yusuf laughed again, then typed the warning for next time.

qa.q: Where was Rehana when Yusuf's voice notes arrived?
qa.a: Rehana was at her aunt's dinner table.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling while recording the voice note?
qa.a: Yusuf was delighted and amused, laughing so hard he had to stop twice, eager to share the funny match with a close friend.

qa.q: What small, kind change did Rehana suggest?
qa.a: She asked him to text a short warning first, like "long voice note, funny, no hurry", so she could choose when and where to listen.

qa.q: What was it like for Rehana when the note played out loud?
qa.a: Rehana felt embarrassed in front of her aunt and cousins, though she still enjoyed the story and felt close to Yusuf 😊

grounding: A teenager sends long laughing voice notes that feel personal, but they assume the friend has time and privacy to listen.

passage:
"Seema! Did you hear my voice note?"
"All six minutes of it, Farida."
"And? Wasn't it the funniest thing? The part where the teacher's chair squeaked?"
"It was funny. I laughed. But I played it in the kitchen."
"So?"
"So my phone was on speaker and Mummy was making rotis. She heard the whole bit about you liking Dev from the science club."
"No. No, no, no."
"Yes. She asked who Dev was for ten minutes."
"Seema, I'm so sorry! I just talk and talk when I record, it feels like we're sitting together."
"I know, and I like that. I miss your voice when we don't meet. But maybe put secrets in text, or ask if I'm alone?"
"Deal. Secrets in text. Voice notes only for squeaky chairs."
"And send me the squeaky chair one again. I want to hear it with earphones."

qa.q: How long was Farida's voice note?
qa.a: It was six minutes long.

qa.q: How did Farida feel on learning that Seema's mother had heard?
qa.a: Farida felt embarrassed and sorry, crying "No, no, no" and apologising at once.

qa.q: What small change did the friends agree on?
qa.a: Farida would put secrets in text or check that Seema is alone, and keep voice notes for funny, safe stories.

qa.q: What do Farida's voice notes mean to Seema?
qa.a: Seema enjoys them and feels close to Farida, missing Farida's voice when they don't meet, even though this one caused an awkward moment.

grounding: A teenager's rambling voice notes feel personal and close, but assume the friend has privacy to listen.

passage:
My name is Naveen, and I used to send Rukmini voice notes at night the way other people send full stops. Two minutes, five minutes, once eleven. I'd lie on the terrace and ramble about the maths teacher's new moustache, a song stuck in my head, whether dogs dream. I'd laugh at my own jokes halfway through. It felt closer than typing, like she was right there.
Then one day at the bus stop, Rukmini said, "I love your notes. But I share a room with my two sisters, so I listen in the bathroom with the tap running, at double speed."
I didn't know whether to laugh or hide. Double speed! All my careful pauses!
We worked it out. I still send them, but shorter, and I start with "no rush". She sends a heart when she's heard it, whenever that is.
Sometimes I still send a long one. She says those are her weekend listening.

qa.q: Where did Rukmini listen to the voice notes?
qa.a: Rukmini listened in the bathroom with the tap running, at double speed.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling when Rukmini explained how she listened?
qa.a: Naveen felt embarrassed and amused at once, not sure whether to laugh or hide at the thought of the careful pauses played at double speed.

qa.q: What change worked for both of them?
qa.a: Naveen kept sending notes but made them shorter and started with "no rush", and Rukmini replied with a heart once she'd heard them.

qa.q: What would change if Rukmini had her own room?
qa.a: She could enjoy the long notes calmly at normal speed, and they would feel less like a secret squeezed into the bathroom.

grounding: A teenager's long rambling voice notes feel intimate, but assume the friend has time and privacy to listen.

passage: Trip note, Class 11 excursion bus to Mysuru, Saturday. Elizabeth spent the ride recording voice notes for Imran, who had stayed home unwell. They were long and happy: the monkey that stole Rhea's chips, the bus horn that plays a tune, and laughter so hard she had to restart twice. One note ran over six minutes. Around noon her face fell. Imran had texted: "lol I can hear you laughing in the preview but I'm in the doctor's waiting room with my dad, can't play these. text me the monkey part?" Elizabeth said to me, a little embarrassed, "I didn't even think he might not be able to listen." We talked about sending a one-line text first, such as "long funny voice note coming, listen later?" She typed a short summary with a monkey 🐒. That evening Imran replied that he had played them all in bed and laughed until his dad came to check.

qa.q: How long did one of the notes run?
qa.a: One note ran over six minutes.

qa.q: Why did Elizabeth's face fall around noon?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and a bit let down, realising Imran could not play her notes in the doctor's waiting room.

qa.q: What small habit could Elizabeth try before sending a long voice note?
qa.a: Send a one-line text first, like "long funny voice note coming, listen later?", or add a short written summary so the friend can choose when to listen.

qa.q: What were the voice notes like for Imran once he could listen?
qa.a: They let him share a trip he had missed; he played them all in bed and laughed hard 😊

grounding: Shows a teenager sending long, laughing voice notes to a close friend, which feel personal but assume the friend has time and privacy to listen.
